subject: Renewal flexibility and billing latch — MedStream
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@medstream.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal options for Q4 uplift

Hi David,

Thanks for the call earlier — quick follow up from our side. Our usage is pacing +45% QoQ and Procurement wants clarity on two things before we can sign the renewal amendment: 1) an option to co-term the uplift to align with our other vendors and 2) a billing "latch" so the increased committed units can be invoiced over the remainder of our current term rather than starting a new invoice cycle.

Can you share a couple of structured options (one conservative, one aggressive) and confirm whether Redwood can absorb a small one-time discount if we commit to the higher commit for 12 months? Also attaching the current SOW so Legal can see the exact scope.

Best,
Samir
Head of Platform
MedStream AI

Attachment: MedStream_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@medstream.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options for Q4 uplift

Hi Samir — really appreciate the context and the SOW.

Short answer: yes, we can do both co-terming and a billing latch. I've attached two proposal tables: a conservative uplift (40% commit increase, no upfront credit, 6-month ramp, 6% volume discount) and an aggressive uplift (70% commit increase, 1-month credit applied, 10% volume discount, 12-month commitment). See redwood-pricing-grid.xlsx.

Important operational notes:
- Co-term: we can pro-rate the remaining months to sync the renewal date — no system changes required.
- Billing latch: we can apply the increased committed units to invoices issued during the remaining term and amortize any one-time credit across those invoices so it doesn't create duplicate billing cycles.
- Legal/Procurement: small redlines acceptable; we prefer a single execution (DocuSign) to keep sign-off fast.

I'm looping in Lauren to confirm finance & invoicing cadence, and we can also bring in Irene for draft contract language if you want a pre-redline PDF tonight.

Next steps I suggest: 1) pick conservative vs aggressive, 2) confirm preferred signer (PO or DocuSign), 3) we'll send an amendment + draft invoice schedule.

Thanks — talk soon.

David Kim
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-pricing-grid.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: MedStream — suggested concession path

David / Lauren — quick internal note before we send to Samir.

I reviewed the usage graphs and the proposed pricing grid. My recommendation:
- Offer the aggressive uplift only if MedStream signs a 12-month committed uplift (deal_id RDW-2345-MED) and agrees to the amortized credit on the August–December invoices. That gets us predictable revenue and avoids invoicing churn.
- Approve a limited one-time concession: 5% extra discount applied to months 1–3 as a "welcome ramp" (on top of the 10% volume) but cap total concession value to <$25k. This is palatable to finance given their growth signal.
- For procurement language: include explicit wording that the billing latch applies to invoiced periods within the current term and that any overage above the committed units will follow standard overage rates.

Lauren — can you confirm that accounting can split the amortized credit across the remaining term and still produce clean AR entries? If yes, we can finalize the amendment and route to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Irene
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@medstream.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medstream.ai
Date: 2026-08-31T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options for Q4 uplift

David — thanks, this is helpful and aligned with what Procurement expected. We prefer the aggressive uplift with the 12-month commitment and the amortized credit cadence. Procurement will sign via DocuSign; please send the amendment and an invoice schedule so our finance team can map to our internal ledger.

Couple of small asks before DocuSign:
- Can you add the exact cap language for the one-time concession ("not to exceed USD 25,000")?
- In the amendment, add a sentence clarifying that the billing latch applies only to committed units and that overage rates remain unchanged.

If you can get a DocuSign packet with those two lines added, I'll route it to our CFO for signature. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Samir
